Pattern: Receipt/acknowledgement guard breaks new-consumer/old-provider compatibility (Python, settings-save protocol; enhanced-settings Task 1).

Smell: A client increment adds an UNCONDITIONAL positive-acknowledgement check on a provider response field that only a newer, not-yet-released provider emits — e.g. `if response.get("applied") is not True: raise RuntimeError(...)`. The released/supported provider returns only `{"ok": True}` (no `applied` key), so the check raises on every ordinary save even though the provider actually persisted the values. P0 regression against a hard "independently releasable main / must support released provider" delivery contract.

Why non-obvious: the unit test is updated in the SAME diff to return the NEW provider's response shape (`{"ok": True, "applied": True}`), so the suite stays green and masks the regression. Green implementation-shaped tests do not prove the business operation against the SUPPORTED baseline.

Detection: when a consumer starts requiring a response field as part of a multi-repo/phased rollout, trace it against the released provider blob (not the candidate provider, not the mock). Absent-field tolerance is the compatibility question.

Fix shape: treat absent acknowledgement as legacy success; only fail on explicit negative — `if response.get("applied") is False: raise ...`. Add a test using the released-provider response shape (no `applied` key) asserting success.
